stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion?
stimulus: An agronomist wanted to estimate the mean wheat yield, in bushels per acre, for all wheat farms in a state. The agronomist randomly selected 40 farms from the membership list of the state's Irrigated Grain Growers Cooperative, which accepts only farms that irrigate their fields. The mean yield of the selected farms was 72 bushels per acre.
choices: Because the farms were chosen at random, 72 bushels per acre is a sound estimate for all wheat farms in the state.
The only problem is size; randomly choosing 400 cooperative farms would give a sound estimate for the whole state.
The farms were chosen at random from irrigated farms only, so the estimate may be biased for all farms in the state.
Randomly choosing 40 farms that do not irrigate would give a sound estimate of the mean yield for the whole state.
explanation: The agronomist wants to know about all wheat farms in the state. The farms were chosen at random, but only from a cooperative that accepts irrigated farms. Random selection lets you generalize only to the group you selected from, which here is irrigated cooperative farms. Irrigated farms may yield more than farms that rely on rain, so the estimate may be biased for the state as a whole.

A.why: You saw the word 'random' and stopped there. The farms were chosen at random from irrigated cooperative farms only, so the result can't be stretched to every wheat farm in the state.

B.why: You blamed the sample size. Choosing 400 farms from the same irrigated-only list still leaves out every farm that doesn't irrigate, so the bias stays.

D.why: You swapped one subgroup for its opposite. Farms that don't irrigate are no more representative of all farms than irrigated farms are.

A.why: You worked out 150 ÷ 200 = 75% correctly and then applied it to the whole town. A large majority in a self-selected group of festival-goers doesn't tell you about everyone else.

C.why: You blamed the sample size. Asking 2,000 people at the same parade repeats the same selection problem on a larger scale.

stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion about the survey results?
stimulus: A county science center wanted to estimate the percentage of adults in the county who have seen the Milky Way with the naked eye. Staff surveyed 250 adults attending a stargazing night at a rural observatory, and 92% said they had.
choices: About 92% of the county's adults have seen the Milky Way with the naked eye.
The results may not represent the county, since the adults were not chosen at random.
The results would represent the county if 500 attendees had been surveyed instead.
The results would represent the county if only city residents had been surveyed.
explanation: The question is about all adults in the county, but the sample came from a stargazing night at a dark rural site. People who go to such an event are much more likely than a typical adult to have seen the Milky Way. This is a convenience sample of an interested subgroup, not a random sample of county adults, so the 92% may overstate the true percentage.

A.why: You treated a large majority in a biased sample as proof about the whole county. A result from stargazing-night attendees cannot be applied to all adults in the county.

C.why: You blamed the sample size instead of how the sample was chosen. Surveying 500 stargazing-night attendees would still sample only that group, so the bias would remain.

D.why: You swapped one unrepresentative subgroup for another. City residents live under brighter skies, so a sample of only them would probably miss in the other direction. Neither group is a random sample of the county.

stem: Which of the following statements about the method used is true?
stimulus: An aquarium wanted to know what percentage of its annual members would pay for a behind-the-scenes shark tour. It placed a touchscreen poll beside the shark tank, and any visitor could choose to answer. Of the 300 visitors who answered, 70% said yes.
choices: It is flawed because 300 responses are too few to give a reliable estimate.
It is flawed because the respondents chose themselves at the shark tank.
It is flawed because it should have polled only visitors who skip the sharks.
It is sound because a clear majority of the respondents answered yes.
explanation: The aquarium wants to learn about its annual members. Its respondents, though, were visitors who happened to be at the shark tank and decided to answer. That makes the sample self-selected, and it may include people who are not members at all. Visitors standing at the shark tank are also likely to be more interested in sharks than a typical member. The sample is not random, so the 70% may be biased.

A.why: You blamed the sample size instead of how the sample was chosen. Three hundred randomly chosen members could give a useful estimate. The problem is that these respondents picked themselves at the shark tank.

C.why: You accepted a fix that swaps one unrepresentative subgroup for its opposite. Visitors who skip the sharks are no more a random sample of members than visitors who stop at the tank.

D.why: You treated a clear majority as proof the method works. A large percentage cannot make up for a self-selected sample, so 70% says nothing reliable about all annual members.

stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion?
stimulus: A music historian wants to estimate the percentage of all concert-goers in a city who prefer Baroque music to Romantic music. The historian surveyed 400 people as they left a weekend Baroque music festival in the city, and 82% of them said they prefer Baroque music.
choices: Because 400 people were surveyed, about 82% of the city's concert-goers prefer Baroque music.
The result may be biased because everyone surveyed had chosen to attend a Baroque festival.
The result would represent the city's concert-goers if 400 more festival attendees were surveyed.
The result would represent the city's concert-goers if the survey were given at a Romantic concert.
explanation: The historian wants to learn about all concert-goers in the city, but the sample came only from people leaving a Baroque festival. Those people chose to go to Baroque music, so they are more likely than other concert-goers to prefer it. The sample was not chosen at random from the whole population, so the 82% figure may be biased.

A.why: You treated a large majority in a large sample as proof about everyone. Surveying more people does not help if they were all picked from a group that already leans toward Baroque music.

C.why: You blamed the sample size. The problem is where the sample came from, and adding more festival attendees just adds more people from the same lopsided group.

D.why: You swapped one unrepresentative group for its opposite. People at a Romantic concert lean the other way, so that sample would be biased in the other direction.

stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion?
stimulus: A linguist wants to estimate the proportion of adults in a region who speak two or more languages. The linguist posted a questionnaire on a popular language-learning website, and 1,200 adults from the region who visited the site chose to fill it out. Of these, 71% reported speaking two or more languages.
choices: Because over 1,000 adults responded, about 71% of the region's adults speak two or more languages.
The respondents chose to respond on a language site, so they may not represent the region's adults.
The sample of 1,200 adults is too small to support any conclusion about the region's adults.
Most adults in the region who speak two or more languages visit language-learning websites.
explanation: The population is all adults in the region, but the sample is visitors to a language-learning website who decided to answer for themselves. People who visit that kind of site, and who choose to answer a questionnaire about languages, are more likely than most adults to speak more than one. The sample is self-selected rather than random, so it may not represent the region.

A.why: You applied the sample's 71% to the whole region. A big self-selected sample is still self-selected, and its size does not cancel out the bias.

C.why: You blamed the sample size. 1,200 is plenty for a random sample. What's wrong here is how the respondents were gathered, not how many there were.

D.why: You reversed the relationship. The data describe site visitors who answered the questionnaire, not what share of all multilingual adults visit such sites. Nothing in the study measures that.

stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion?
stimulus: A county weather service wants to know whether county residents think severe-storm warnings are issued too often. The service surveyed 160 owners of businesses in the county that run outdoor events, which are often canceled when a warning is issued. Of these owners, 120 said warnings are issued too often.
choices: Since 75% of those surveyed agreed, most county residents think warnings are issued too often.
The results may be biased, since outdoor-event owners lose money when warnings are issued.
The results would represent the county if 160 more outdoor-event business owners were surveyed.
The results would represent the county if only residents who own no business were surveyed.
explanation: The service wants to learn about all county residents, but it surveyed only outdoor-event business owners. That group loses money when warnings cancel events, so it has a stake in the answer and is likely to say warnings come too often. The sample is a special subgroup rather than a random sample of residents, so the results may be biased.

A.why: You worked out 120 out of 160 = 75% and applied it to the whole county. A clear majority in a biased sample tells you about that subgroup, not about all residents.

C.why: You blamed the sample size. Surveying more event owners still leaves out every other resident, so the bias stays.

D.why: You swapped one unrepresentative group for another. Leaving out every business owner means the sample is still not randomly chosen from all residents.
